From X-rays to detector counts

Simulate a 30 keV beam on 100 nm HOPG and acquire an ideal pixel image. The 16 × 16 pixel panel sits 100 mm away at 135°; 0.01 pC bunches at 1 MHz give 10 nA average current.

Define the observation

Scene defines the geometry; Observation specifies response, exposure and angular sampling. IdealPhotonCounter has unit efficiency and no energy broadening. Count photons in [0.5, 4) keV over 1 s using a seeded Poisson draw. The 4 × 4 angular tiles are the source-scoring resolution, not the 16 × 16 detector pixels.

Interpretation

Both images already include beam current, exposure, pixel solid angle and ideal response. Do not rescale them again. They include CXR, bremsstrahlung and characteristic photons within the reporting window; no downstream filter or background is modeled. The left panel is an expected count image; the right is one Poisson realization. The shared color scale exposes counting noise, but does not include Monte Carlo uncertainty or calibration effects. Try changing only acquisition.seed, then doubling exposure_s. Counts vary with the seed; expectations scale with exposure. See the detector how-to and response physics.
